searchText: i'm curious what lessons so far have been learned from Madella and where do we go next? is it operating as we hoped? how does it bode for mainnet release? has it been thru hardening tests? I think the goal is to let it run for a longer duration, meanwhile iron out the kinks in the clients? eg. I know nimbus and lodestar (I think?) were not running especially well at the very beginning, that was part of why we started with only 57% uptime for an hour or so; I'm sure they're improving a lot now thanks <@!273808422753796097> I know in the past there were talks about trying different "bad network" environment tests on ETH2, are those going to be performed on Medalla to see how we fair? also curious if there is going to be any mechanism one could test ahead of time when depositing, that your withdrawl keys are going to work 2 years later down the road? (ie accessibility to your deposited funds later down the road) On medalla, we will ensure we run through a complete list of all "expected" behaviours wrt consensus state transitions (exits, slashings, empty blocks, full blocks, etc). In addition to Medalla, we are running a series of "attack nets" on which white hat hackers are bringing networks down for bounties (https://github.com/ethresearch/public-attacknets) And in addition to that, we are subjecting each client to a series of load tests under various scenarios (starting a few weeks from now) The Launchpad, automatically tests the validity of withdrawal credentials before allowing the user to submit deposits making a dedicated page for all users (regardless of launchpad deposits or not) to test their withdrawal credentials probably makes sense thank you <@!291925846556540928> appreciate the thorough response <@291925846556540928> are we planning to come up with a checklist of items that need to be crossed off for mainnet release?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
On medalla, we will ensure we run through a complete list of all "expected" behaviours wrt consensus state transitions (exits, slashings, empty blocks, full blocks, etc).

In addition to Medalla, we are running a series of "attack nets" on which white hat hackers are bringing networks down for bounties (https://github.com/ethresearch/public-attacknets)

And in addition to that, we are subjecting each client to a series of load tests under various scenarios (starting a few weeks from now)

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: The Launchpad, automatically tests the validity of withdrawal credentials before allowing the user to submit deposits

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: making a dedicated page for all users (regardless of launchpad deposits or not) to test their withdrawal credentials probably makes sense
